forest_planting.title: CAFSD Graduands Plant Native Trees and Bamboo in the University Forest Reserves
paras: Some 230 graduating students of the College of Agriculture, Food and Sustainable Development (CAFSD) of Mariano Marcos State University (MMSU) planted trees and bamboo in the University Forest Reserves in Barangays Payao and Mabaleng, City of Batac, on July 2, 2025. The activity was led by CAFSD OIC-Dean Charlie Batin and the 2025 CAFSD Graduating Class Student Council, with Dr. Joselito Rosario, Director for Agribusiness, and Mr. Bonne Jovie Orteza of the MMSU Bamboo Research and Development Center. MMSU President Virgilio Julius P. Manzano Jr. commended the class for leaving a lasting green footprint that will further preserve the forest areas managed by the university, and Mr. Hashler Garalde, a CAFSD alumnus representing the Provincial Government of Ilocos Norte, supported the college’s sustainability efforts.

The graduands planted 120 seedlings of guijo and yakal, native dipterocarp timber species raised at the MMSU Central Nursery, in the Payao Forest Reserve, and 130 propagules of kawayan tinik, machiku and giant bamboo from the MMSU Bamboo Nursery in Mabaleng.

forest_reserve.title: Enriching MMSU’s 1,068-Hectare Forest Reserves with Native Species
paras: MMSU manages Forest Reserve Areas in Barangays Lubbot and Payao, City of Batac, covering a total of 1,068.13 hectares, where the university’s forestry and agroforestry research is set up. The university maintains and extends these ecosystems with planting stock raised in its own nurseries, the MMSU Central Nursery and the MMSU Bamboo Nursery.

On July 2, 2025, 230 CAFSD graduating students enriched the reserves with 120 seedlings of the native dipterocarps guijo and yakal in Payao and 130 propagules of kawayan tinik, machiku and giant bamboo in Mabaleng. The activity was led by CAFSD OIC-Dean Charlie Batin with the MMSU Bamboo Research and Development Center.

ifp_conservation.title: Conserving Ilocos Indigenous Food Plants In Situ, Ex Situ and Circa Situ
paras: Through its Indigenous Food Plants (IFP) Program, MMSU conserves the wild and neglected food plants of Ilocos Norte, 46 of which were documented by the program in seven towns of the province. The program follows a triad of conservation approaches: an IFP Botanical Garden for ex situ conservation, a himbabao (alukon) genebank at the MMSU Forest Reserve, circa situ cultivation of the wild yams kamangeg and dolian, and the integration of IFPs into community foodscapes.

In October 2025, in celebration of World Food Day, the MMSU Extension and Research Directorates established the second batch of Community Foodscapes and Seedbanks for Indigenous Food Plants with local government units and schools, at Eladio V. Barangan Memorial Elementary School in San Nicolas, Ilocos Norte. The foodscape sites serve as seedbanks and learning gardens, and partner communities receive planting materials and technical assistance to cultivate kapaskapas, alokon, pako, dalayap, wild singkamas and roselle. The new partners join existing foodscape sites in Sarrat and Batac.

The IFP Program was adopted by the Regional Development Council of Region 1 as its first research and development initiative, and a study on the program by Dr. Menisa A. Antonio and co-authors won Best Paper in the Sustainable and Smart Agri-Aquaculture and Climate Resilience category of the SUC-ACAP 2025 Biennial Conference, held August 27–29, 2025, in Tagbilaran City, Bohol.

mangrove_nbs.title: Nature-based Solutions for Mangrove Ecosystems in Badoc and Currimao
paras: Throughout 2025, MMSU implemented the DOST-PCAARRD-funded project “Nature-based Solutions (NbS) for Sustainable Mangrove Management and Resilient Coastal Communities Through Innovative Green Engineering Approach,” led by Dr. Arlene L. Gonzales, in Badoc and Currimao, Ilocos Norte, with DENR-PENRO Ilocos Norte, the Provincial Government of Ilocos Norte and the LGUs of Badoc and Currimao. The project uses green engineering and locally available, ecologically friendly materials, including bamboo-engineered structures that protect young mangroves and improve their survival.

In 2025, MMSU and DENR Region 1 met at ILAARRDEC to advance the work, with DENR pledging technical support and active participation in restoration, monitoring and evaluation, and the project trained representatives of Currimao, Pasuquin, Badoc and Burgos in mangrove propagation, management and conservation on October 27–28, 2025.

idbd_contest.title: 2025 International Day for Biological Diversity Wildlife Photo Contest
paras: MMSU, through its Office of Sustainability and Futures Thinking, marked the 2025 International Day for Biological Diversity with a Wildlife Photo Contest that invited the university community to document local wildlife and promote awareness of biodiversity conservation. Entrants followed animal-photography ethical guidelines: avoiding flash and loud noises, never using bait or food lures, following local laws and warning signs, keeping clear of nesting sites and sensitive habitats, and captioning photographs honestly. Entries were received until May 30, 2025.

Chris Jeremiah C. Antonio, a third-year BA Communication student, was named winner and received a ₱1,000 gift voucher and a certificate from Dr. Arlene L. Gonzales, Chief of Sustainability and Futures Thinking.

mangrove_seminar.title: MMSU Trains Coastal Towns on Mangrove Propagation, Management and Conservation
paras: MMSU conducted a two-day Seminar-Workshop on Mangrove Propagation on October 27–28, 2025 at its Center for Flexible Learning for representatives of the coastal municipalities of Currimao, Pasuquin, Badoc and Burgos, Ilocos Norte, with officials of DENR-PENRO in attendance. The training was organized under the DOST-PCAARRD-funded nature-based solutions mangrove project led by Dr. Arlene Gonzales.

Sessions covered the importance of mangrove ecosystems, nature-based solutions for conservation, legal frameworks for mangrove protection, and the roles of the academe and local government units in community-based mangrove management. Participants were also trained in nursery management and advanced propagation techniques for Avicennia and Sonneratia species and other local mangrove varieties. The Pedada People’s Organization shared its experience in establishing community-based mangrove conservation.

alukon.title: Farmers in Sarrat Trained to Propagate the Indigenous Alukon
paras: On May 2, 2025, the MMSU Research and Extension Directorates trained 64 farmers in Barangay 11 Sta. Rosa, Sarrat, Ilocos Norte, on the propagation of alukon (himbabao), a Philippine indigenous vegetable tree. Barangay officials, members of the Task Force Dagger Special Operations Foundation and representatives of the local government unit also attended. The training was held in response to requests from the community.

Resource speakers Dr. Menisa Antonio, Engr. Josefa Pugat and Mr. Jayson Rasay of the Research Directorate presented recommended propagation strategies to establish sustained alukon production in the community and broaden the use of the crop for food and other applications.

ifp_learning.title: Community Foodscapes as Learning Gardens for Indigenous Plants
paras: In October 2025, in celebration of World Food Day, the MMSU Extension and Research Directorates established the second batch of Community Foodscapes and Seedbanks for Indigenous Food Plants at Eladio V. Barangan Memorial Elementary School, San Nicolas, Ilocos Norte. Barangay officials of San Roque and Parut, Vintar, agricultural extension workers, school leaders and community representatives took part.

The foodscape sites serve as seedbanks and learning gardens that encourage knowledge sharing and sustainable farming practices. Communities receive planting materials and technical assistance to cultivate indigenous crops such as kapaskapas, alokon, pako, dalayap, wild singkamas and roselle, conserving indigenous food resources across Ilocos Norte.

pinili.title: Bamboo Propagation and Plantation Management Training in Pinili
paras: The MMSU Extension Directorate and the College of Agriculture, Food and Sustainable Development, in partnership with Barangay Aglipay, Pinili, Ilocos Norte, and with the support of the Ilocos Agriculture, Aquatic and Natural Resources Research and Development Consortium (ILAARRDEC), conducted a two-day training on bamboo production in 2025.

The training equipped 46 farmers, local leaders and community members with practical skills in bamboo propagation, nursery establishment and plantation management. Lectures covered the prospects of the bamboo industry and MMSU’s propagation methods, and participants helped establish a new bambusetum, a collection of bamboo species, in Barangay Aglipay. Lectures and demonstrations were given by bamboo experts Mr. Charlie Maine Cacactin of CAFSD and Mr. Bonne Jovie Orteza of MMSU. Pinili Municipal Agriculturist Philip Galang, representing Mayor Rommel T. Labasan, thanked MMSU and ILAARRDEC, and the project was championed in the community by Pinili’s Magsasaka Siyentista, Mr. Reynaldo Antalan.

pinili_short.title: A New Bambusetum in Barangay Aglipay, Pinili
paras: During a two-day bamboo production training in 2025, the MMSU Extension Directorate and CAFSD, with Barangay Aglipay, Pinili, and the support of ILAARRDEC, worked with 46 farmers, local leaders and community members to establish a new bambusetum, a collection of bamboo species, in Barangay Aglipay. The training covered bamboo propagation, nursery establishment and plantation management.

pasuquin.title: MMSU, TMP Foundation, DENR and Pasuquin LGU Sign Agreement to Conserve a Coastal Forest
paras: On November 29, 2025, Mariano Marcos State University, the Toyota Motor Philippines Foundation (TMPF), the Department of Environment and Natural Resources and the Local Government Unit of Pasuquin formalized through a memorandum of agreement a partnership to strengthen coastal forest conservation in Barangay Davila, Pasuquin, Ilocos Norte. The agreement was signed by MMSU President Virgilio Julius P. Manzano Jr. with TMPF leadership, Toyota Motor Philippines and Toyota Ilocos Norte executives, DENR-CENRO Bangui Ecosystem Management Specialist Justine Rose Teneza, and Sangguniang Bayan Member Romel Ranay for LGU-Pasuquin.

A mangrove planting followed the signing, with 1,750 propagules planted and another 1,750 planned for the following year. TMPF President Jose Maria Aligada described the partnership as shared stewardship to restore native mangrove species, rehabilitate coastal systems and boost community resilience to climate-related hazards. Former MMSU College of Industrial Technology Dean Cesario Pacis was recognized as one of the initiators of the MMSU–Toyota partnership.

denr_partnership.title: MMSU and DENR Region 1 Strengthen Partnership for Mangrove Conservation
paras: MMSU, in partnership with the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) Region 1, convened a dialogue at ILAARRDEC to advance mangrove conservation and coastal resilience in the Ilocos Region through science-based and community-centered approaches. Central to the dialogue was the DOST-PCAARRD-funded nature-based solutions mangrove project led by Dr. Arlene Gonzales.

DENR officials pledged technical support and active participation in restoration, monitoring and evaluation activities. The same project brought representatives of Currimao, Pasuquin, Badoc and Burgos, with DENR-PENRO, to MMSU’s mangrove propagation seminar-workshop on October 27–28, 2025.

ifp_partners.title: Indigenous Food Plant Foodscapes Established with Vintar and San Nicolas Partners
paras: In October 2025, the MMSU Extension and Research Directorates partnered with local government units and schools to establish Community Foodscapes and Seedbanks for Indigenous Food Plants. Held at Eladio V. Barangan Memorial Elementary School in San Nicolas, Ilocos Norte, the activity brought together officials of Barangays San Roque and Parut, Vintar, the Municipal Agriculture Office of Vintar, agricultural extension workers, school leaders and community representatives as the second batch of partner sites.

The partner communities maintain the foodscapes as shared seedbanks and learning gardens, with planting materials and technical assistance from MMSU, to conserve indigenous food resources such as kapaskapas, alokon, pako, dalayap, wild singkamas and roselle. They join existing foodscape sites in Sarrat and Batac.

rec.title: MMSU Commits to the DENR-EMB Region I Regional Ecology Center
paras: On July 1, 2025, in Bauang, La Union, MMSU signed a memorandum of commitment with the DENR–Environmental Management Bureau Region I and other government agencies, private sector representatives, non-government organizations and academic institutions for the Regional Ecology Center. MMSU was represented by Vice President for Planning and Strategic Foresight Mee Jay Domingo and Campus Sustainability Chief Ronnel Pagurayan.

Under the commitment, MMSU supports improved solid waste management under Republic Act 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act) and Republic Act 11898 (Extended Producer Responsibility Act) through education and public information campaigns and the development of informational materials.

soa.title: School-on-the-Air Brings Regenerative Vegetable Farming to 1,000 Ilocanos
paras: A new season of the MMSU School-on-the-Air (SOA), the university’s radio-based educational program, opened on June 24 and 25, 2025 with 1,000 enrollees from the 22 municipalities and cities of Ilocos Norte. The season focused on regenerative vegetable farming for enhanced and sustainable production, with lessons on climate-smart practices and off-season vegetable seeding.

Vegetable growers, rural improvement club members, agricultural extension workers and students followed the lessons, broadcast from June to December 2025 over DWFB Radyo Pilipinas Laoag, DWCI Radyo Adjo Piddig and DWNI Radyo Karruba Burgos. MMSU ran the program with the Provincial Government of Ilocos Norte, the Office of the Provincial Agriculturist, local government units, the Ilocos Agriculture, Aquatic and Natural Resources Research and Development Consortium, and the High-Value Crops Division of Ilocos Norte.

fieldday.title: President’s Farm Field Day Showcases Climate-Resilient Rice Varieties
paras: On October 28, 2025, the MMSU Extension Directorate, with the Philippine Rice Research Institute (PhilRice) Batac Branch, held the President’s Farm Field Day: A Technology Showcase in front of the College of Agriculture, Food and Sustainable Development. Farmers and farmer-leaders, agricultural technicians from Ilocos Norte local government units, BS Agriculture students, and MMSU and PhilRice rice specialists viewed eight rice varieties grown under wet-season conditions.

The varieties included four newly released by PhilRice, two public hybrids, and two suited to saline and rainfed conditions, among them NSIC Rc 686 (Salinas 39) and NSIC Rc 650 (Sahod Ulan 36), giving farmers options for saline-affected and rainfed fields. Speakers included MMSU President Dr. Virgilio Julius P. Manzano Jr., Extension Director Dr. Marlowe Aquino, and former MMSU President and PhilRice Executive Director Dr. Santiago R. Obien.

sirmata.title: Sirmata 2040: Planning MMSU’s Campuses and Reserve Lands for Two Decades
paras: Sirmata 2040, MMSU’s Land Use Development and Infrastructure Plan (LUDIP), is the university’s 20-year guide for managing its land resources and infrastructure. Prepared under Republic Act 11396, which requires state universities and colleges to have a LUDIP, and supported by a Php 2 million grant from the Commission on Higher Education (CHED), the plan covers the future land use of the MMSU campuses and the university’s reserve areas in Nagbacsan, Payao, Lubbot and Sarnap, City of Batac, including the forest reserves where MMSU’s forestry and agroforestry research is set up.

Local biodiversity is built into the plan’s development rules. The zoning plan sets aside Protected Land, which “shall be conserved, preserved and to be excluded from any form of alteration except as may be permitted by operation of law” (Policy 9.1), and the MMSU Forest Reserve is kept as a no-build zone. Before any land is altered or converted, the plan requires a science-based assessment of its natural suitability and carrying capacity (Policies 7.1, 10.1 and 11.1).
The plan was developed through stakeholder consultations, sectoral studies and campus planning workshops, and was endorsed by the CHED Technical Working Group after validation visits to the campuses.

landuse_policy.title: MMSU Land Use Policy Commits the University to Conserve and Restore Its Lands
paras: MMSU’s Land Use, Zoning, Water and Energy Policies, adopted as part of Sirmata 2040, the university’s Land Use Development and Infrastructure Plan prepared in 2021 under Republic Act 11396, govern the conservation, restoration and sustainable use of all university lands across its campuses.

Under Policy 1.3, the allocation and use of university lands “shall aim to maintain, protect, conserve, restore, and enhance the integrity of the land itself, the environment and ecological balance in all its campuses.” Policy 7.1 requires decisions to be based on valid and reliable science, especially for any intent to alter or convert the natural state of any piece of university land, and Policy 10.2 gives fragile lands and protected areas special management “to protect, conserve, enrich, rehabilitate, and or sustain them.”

The zoning policy sets aside Protected Land as a distinct zone; under Policy 9.1, “protected landholdings of the university shall be conserved, preserved and to be excluded from any form of alteration except as may be permitted by operation of law.” The MMSU Forest Reserve is maintained as a no-build zone, and Policy 4.3 requires the university to regularly review, update and promptly communicate its land-use policies.

kpnp.title: MMSU Expert Serves on the Kalbario-Patapat Natural Park Technical Working Group
paras: Through DENR-PENRO Ilocos Norte Special Order No. 2023-024, dated March 29, 2023, Dr. Arlene L. Gonzales of MMSU was named a member of the Technical Working Group that prepares the Communication Plan of the Kalbario-Patapat Natural Park (KPNP), a protected area in Ilocos Norte. The group, led by the KPNP Protected Area Superintendent, brings together DENR offices, the Provincial Government of Ilocos Norte, the LGUs of Pagudpud and Adams in Ilocos Norte and Sta. Praxedes in Cagayan, barangay officials and Northwestern University.

The Communication Plan supports the goal of the KPNP Protected Area Management Plan to adopt and carry out effective information and education campaigns for biological diversity conservation and for the promotion of the protected area as a major ecotourism destination.

water.title: Groundwater Quality Monitoring at the MMSU Farm
paras: Through June 2025, MMSU continued monthly monitoring of 17 groundwater wells on the MMSU Farm, measuring pH, total dissolved solids, electrical conductivity, chloride and nitrate-nitrogen and comparing the results with the Philippine National Standards for Drinking Water (2017). The assessment, covering February 2024 to June 2025, flags wells with persistently high dissolved solids, which rose again from January to May 2025, for continued monitoring to guide water resource management and prevent further degradation of groundwater quality.

plastic.title: MMSU Policies Eliminate Styrofoam and Reduce Plastic Waste on Campus
paras: MMSU reduces plastic waste under its Integrated Waste Management Program, approved by the Board of Regents in 2009 and amended in 2015, and its revised Integrated Pollution and Waste Management Program. The program prohibits Styrofoam for serving or packing food in the university Food Service Unit and limits the use of plastics, and a policy promulgated on February 11, 2016 eliminates Styrofoam and plastic as secondary packaging materials in favour of paper bags, cartons, eco-bags and reusable containers. The University Waste Management Committee develops, reviews and monitors these rules, and the food service unit requires customers dining out to bring their own food containers.

The Office of the President reissues the “No Bottled Water” Policy each year: Memorandum No. 22-148A of April 24, 2022 and Memorandum No. 23-189 of April 24, 2023 stop the serving of bottled water at Administrative Council meetings, ask members to bring their own water containers, and encourage all offices to adopt the same policy. In October 2024 the College of Agriculture, Food and Sustainable Development banned plastic bottled water in its auxiliary buildings, and on July 1, 2025 MMSU signed a memorandum of commitment with DENR-EMB Region I for the Regional Ecology Center to support solid waste management under Republic Act 9003 and the Extended Producer Responsibility Act (Republic Act 11898).

hazardous.title: Hazardous Waste Disposal under MMSU’s Integrated Pollution and Waste Management Program
paras: MMSU’s Integrated Waste Management Program was revised in 2020 into the Integrated Pollution and Waste Management Program (IPWMP), implemented by the Pollution Control Unit and the General Services directorate, to cover hazardous materials. The IPWMP assigns focal persons for hazardous wastes (chemical and related wastes), air and water pollution, solid wastes, and PCBs and related industrial wastes, and requires the waste coordinators of every unit to store and label generated hazardous wastes properly before collection.

The program establishes centralized, separate storage facilities for polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) and other hazardous or toxic wastes collected from the campuses, where the wastes are kept for up to one year before disposal through a DENR-accredited transport, storage and disposal facility, in compliance with Republic Act 6969 and its storage guidelines. Units that generate hazardous waste are registered as hazardous waste generators, and the university coordinates with the Environmental Management Bureau of DENR for final collection and disposal.

wed_mangrove.title: MMSU Plants 250 Mangrove Propagules in Currimao on World Environment Day
paras: In June 2025, in celebration of World Environment Day, Mariano Marcos State University planted 250 mangrove propagules along the coastal area of Barangay Maglaoi, Currimao, Ilocos Norte, to restore degraded shorelines, enhance climate resilience and promote sustainable coastal resource management. The activity was spearheaded by the MMSU Sustainability and Futures Thinking (SFT) Office with the Local Government Unit of Currimao and led by Dr. Mee Jay Domingo, Vice President for Planning and Strategic Foresight.

MMSU faculty, education support personnel and students joined representatives of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources, barangay officials, members of local fisherfolk organizations and community members. SFT Director Dr. Arlene Gonzales explained that mangroves were chosen because they act as natural filters that intercept plastic waste from land before it reaches the sea, while absorbing carbon, protecting shorelines from erosion and providing habitat for marine life.

badoc_mangrove.title: MMSU, Rotary Club and Badoc LGU Restore a Typhoon-Damaged Mangrove Stand
paras: On December 6, 2025, Mariano Marcos State University, the Rotary Club of Laoag Sunshine and the Local Government Unit of Badoc planted 280 mangrove propagules in Barangay Pagsanahan, Badoc, Ilocos Norte, to restore a mangrove stand extensively damaged by past typhoons and to ensure the continuity of ecological succession at the site.

The activity was led by MMSU President Virgilio Julius P. Manzano Jr., with the LGU of Badoc headed by Hon. Virgilio M. Calajate and the Rotary Club of Laoag Sunshine under Atty. Zsa Zsa Raval. MMSU’s Vice President for Resource Generation and its Directors for Extension, Curriculum Development and Innovative Learning, and Student Affairs and Development also took part.

coconut_greenwall.title: Green Wall Program: Coconut Seedlings for the Currimao Coastline
paras: On July 24, 2025, MMSU planted coconut seedlings along the Currimao beachfront under its Green Wall Program, with 1,000 seedlings donated by the Philippine Coconut Authority (PCA), to promote environmental sustainability and coastal resilience amid growing climate threats. The activity was held in celebration of the birthday of CHED Chairperson Shirley C. Agrupis, Chair of the MMSU Board of Regents.

MMSU President Virgilio Julius P. Manzano Jr., PCA Ilocos Norte Agriculturist and In-Charge Rose Ann Cabaloan, and university officials and employees took part. CASAT OIC-Dean Pilar Carolyn Pascual highlighted the university’s commitment to protecting coastal ecosystems through the Green Wall project.

vermicast.title: Vermicast Facility Helps Pasuquin Onion Farmers Restore Degraded Soils
paras: In 2025, white onion farmer-leaders Mr. Marcos Palacay and Mr. Markflor Valdez of the Ayat ti Pasuquin Farmer and Irrigators Association established a pilot vermicomposting facility in Pasuquin, Ilocos Norte, under the Agri-Tech Facilitator Program of the Farmers Entrepreneurship Program of MMSU and the Jollibee Group Foundation. The facility uses African night crawlers (Eudrilus eugeniae) to convert biodegradable farm waste into vermicast, an organic fertilizer that improves soil structure, stimulates microbial activity and reduces the need for chemical inputs.

The project responds to soil degradation from prolonged reliance on chemical fertilizers, which the farmers linked to poor soil conditions and low seedling survival, and promotes sustainable solutions for white onion farming in the area.

onion_training.title: Pasuquin Onion Farmers Trained on Good Agricultural Practices
paras: On November 12, 2025, the Municipality of Pasuquin, MMSU and the Jollibee Group Foundation conducted a Pre-Dispersal Training on White Onion Production at the Pasuquin Municipal Hall for farmer beneficiaries of the San Juan Icas Manuel Farmers’ Association. The training covered white onion production technology, good agricultural practices (GAP) and proper farm recording for sustainable and profitable farming.

Farmer participation in the project has doubled from 15 to 30 beneficiaries, with a collective production target of 200 tons of white onion for 2025. The Office of the Provincial Agriculturist provides seeds and planting materials, complementing MMSU’s technical support and capacity development.

soil_health.title: MMSU Leads Soil Health Research for Rice-Based Cropping Systems
paras: In 2025, MMSU became a key partner in a five-year research program led by Griffith University in Australia and funded by the Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research (ACIAR) and DOST-PCAARRD to develop soil knowledge, information and capacity for more productive and sustainable cropping systems in the Philippines (Project SLaM 2023/146). MMSU President Virgilio Julius P. Manzano Jr. pledged the university’s commitment at the inception meeting held March 24–26, 2025 in Balanga City, Bataan.

MMSU leads the project on enhancing the productivity of rice-based cropping systems in Ilocos Norte, Tarlac and Bataan through soil health management. Led by Dr. Janet Villamor, it evaluates nutrient management practices and develops yield-calibrated soil health indices for rice-garlic, rice-rice and rice-onion systems. The kick-off meeting on June 16, 2025 at the MMSU Center for Flexible Learning brought together Griffith University, the country project manager and the provincial agriculturists of Ilocos Norte, Bataan and Tarlac, with visits to project sites in Batac, Vintar and Pasuquin.

regen_forum.title: MMSU Promotes Regenerative Farming at the 2025 NSTW Forum
paras: On November 19, 2025, MMSU Research Director Dr. Dionisio Bucao served as a resource speaker at the forum series of the 2025 National Science and Technology Week held at Northwestern University, Laoag City. He presented regenerative farming approaches that restore soil health, biodiversity and ecosystem function, and emphasized carbon sequestration, improved soil fertility, water conservation and climate resilience through natural processes, as well as how regenerative farming differs from conventional practice.

pshs_visit.title: Science High School Students Learn Sustainable Farming at MMSU’s Demonstration Farm
paras: On September 19, 2025, 59 Grade 11 and 12 students of the Philippine Science High School–Ilocos Region Campus visited MMSU’s Technology Demonstration Farm in Sta. Magdalena, Sarrat, as part of their community immersion program “The Science of Survival: A Community-Based Exploration,” held during National Biotechnology Week. After an orientation at the ILAARRDEC One-Stop Information Shop at MMSU, Extension Director Dr. Marlowe Aquino discussed the role of biotechnology in agriculture and MMSU’s hybrid off-season tomato varieties, and the students observed sustainable farming practices on site.

vintar_caravan.title: MMSU Brings Bamboo and Alukon Propagation to the 2025 Siwawer Farmers’ Festival
paras: Through its Information and Technology Caravan, MMSU’s Research and Extension Directorates joined the 2025 Siwawer Farmers’ Festival and Agro-Trade Fair at the Vintar Public Auditorium on December 3–4, 2025, with an exhibit of university technologies and a series of expert lectures for farmers.

Forester Shena Rose Garcia introduced sustainable bamboo production using MMSU’s one-node cutting technology, and the second day featured a demonstration on the propagation of alukon, an indigenous vegetable tree, facilitated by Ms. Josefa Pugat. Other lectures covered high-yielding glutinous corn varieties, garlic disease management and black garlic.

cleanup.title: Student Advocates Hold Monthly Clean-Up Drive on Campus
paras: On October 24, 2025, the MMSU Advocates for Cultural Development (MACD), an organization representing students from indigenous peoples’ communities, held its monthly clean-up drive, “iPaglilinis,” around the university grounds, the Student Center and parts of the University Lagoon. About 30 bags of waste were collected and segregated into plastic, paper and tin materials.
